title: CHW Loop Parent-to-Child Cooling Load Response
description: Starts the complete Chiller-1 evaporator and condenser paths, establishes AHU/VAV airflow, stages the AHU cooling valve, and removes load so students can trace CHWS, CHWR, flow, coil BTUH, SAT, and zone delivery.

events.description: Open VAV-3 for zone delivery evidence
Apply a partial AHU coil load
Increase coil flow and building heat pickup
Remove the airside load and observe loop coast/pump heat

expected_results: CHW flow appears when pump proof and isolation-valve position establish, even before compressor proof
Opening the AHU valve increases coil flow and load; CHWR rises above CHWS while AHU SAT falls with actuator and coil lag
The second valve stage increases the return delta and thermal load without an instantaneous temperature step
After load removal the finite loop coasts and gains pump/ambient heat rather than snapping CHWS and CHWR together at 55 F
completion_criteria: Student traces chiller prerequisites through common headers, AHU coil, SAT, VAV DAT, and zone response
Student uses flow and temperature delta together instead of treating CHWS alone as proof of useful cooling
instructor_notes: Recommended at 10x for a roughly 42-second demonstration. Outdoor weather is a target with a 60-simulated-second time constant, so observe the transition rather than expecting an impossible instantaneous weather step. Use RESTART for deterministic thermal replay.
student_objectives: Understand CHW loop energy balance and thermal transport
Distinguish pump flow, compressor proof, coil demand, and useful airside cooling
